data.title: Credentials in Group Policy Preferences and SYSVOL
data.summary: Credentials were present in files readable by all domain users, including Group Policy Preferences entries whose encryption key is published by the vendor, and scripts in SYSVOL containing plaintext passwords.
data.description:
SYSVOL is readable by every authenticated domain user by design, since clients must read policy from it. Anything stored there is therefore available to the whole domain.

Group Policy Preferences could set local account passwords, encrypted with an AES key Microsoft published in its own documentation — making the encryption decorative. Although the feature was removed, the files frequently remain in SYSVOL from earlier deployments.

Logon scripts are the other source: mapped drives, service installs and scheduled tasks with credentials inline. The accounts involved are usually service or local administrator accounts shared across many hosts, so one disclosure is broad lateral movement.
data.recommendation:
* Search SYSVOL for `cpassword` and for credentials in scripts, and remove them.
* Rotate every credential that was exposed, on the assumption that it is known.
* Use LAPS for local administrator passwords, and managed service accounts for services.
* Where a script must authenticate, retrieve the secret at runtime from a secrets manager.
* Audit SYSVOL contents periodically; it accumulates.
data.short_recommendation: Remove credentials from SYSVOL and rotate what was exposed.
